notes: Fair Workweek (MCC ch. 6-110) covers employees in retail and six other industries earning <= $33.85/hour or <= $64,945.55/year, at employers with 100+ employees globally (chicago.gov, read 2026-11-06).
Right to rest premium is 1.25x for the entire shift that begins <10 h after the previous day's shift (extra key premium_applies_to='shift').
Minimum wage applies to employers with 4+ employees; rises every July 1.

Predictability pay (MCC 6-110-050(b)): per changed shift inside the 14-day window — added hours (incl. new shift or extension) = 1 h; date/time moved with no loss of hours = 1 h; cut/cancelled with >24 h notice = 1 h; cut/cancelled with <24 h notice = >=50% of the regular rate for the scheduled hours not worked. 'Predictability Pay' is paid hourly at the employee's regular rate (6-110-020).

Exemptions (6-110-050(d)): (2) mutually agreed shift trade or coverage arrangement between covered employees; (3) change mutually agreed by employee and employer and confirmed in writing; (4) employee-requested change confirmed in writing (incl. sick leave). A call-in to cover an absent coworker that the employee accepts by text is exempt under (3); the employee who called out is exempt under (4) if the request is in writing. Employees may decline hours added with <14 days' notice (6-110-050(a)).

'Writing' or 'written' = printed or printable communication incl. email, text message or computer system (MCC 6-110-020, https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-2639928).

Coverage (MCC 6-110-020): 'Employer' = 100+ employees globally (250+ for not-for-profits), 50 of whom are Covered Employees, primarily engaged in a Covered Industry (Retail is one); Restaurants need 30+ locations and 250+ employees globally. Covered Employee: majority of work time in Chicago, in a covered industry, and pay <= the indexed threshold ($26.00/h or $50,000/yr in the code; $33.85/h or $64,945.55/yr per chicago.gov for 2026).

Tipped minimum wage: max_tip_credit_per_hour 4.09 = $17.05 − $12.96 (chicago.gov, read 2026-11-07). Chicago's One Fair Wage ordinance phases the tip credit out by July 1, 2028 (not encoded; future steps need their published amounts).
applies_to='both': Covered Industries include Retail and Restaurants (MCC 6-110-020); Restaurants also need 30+ locations and 250+ employees globally.
excludes_same_day_split=true: MCC 6-110-070 applies to 'a shift that begins less than 10 hours after the end of the previous day's shift' (previous day only).
exemption_applies_to: MCC 6-110-050(d)(3) exempts any 'Work Schedule change that is mutually agreed to ... and is confirmed in writing' — call-ins and extensions alike.

alcohol_service ages (MCC 4-60-140(a), 4-60-143): IL.chicago.minor_prohibited_roles.1 bans under-21 conservatively (the validator cannot check training); a restaurant may lawfully let a trained 18-20-year-old serve drinks prepared/opened by a 21+ employee (not under tavern or late-hour licenses) — if the store confirms training, rule .2 (under 18, no exception) is the floor. Under-21s may work as hosts/hostesses in restaurants but not handle alcohol. At premises whose principal business is alcohol sales (taverns), under-21s may not work at all while open.

params.exemption_note: Exempt: "A Work Schedule change that is mutually agreed to by the Covered Employee and Employer and is confirmed in writing"; "writing" includes "text message" (MCC 6-110-050(d)(3), 6-110-020).

rules.summary: Inside 14 days, Chicago Fair Workweek pays 1 hour at the regular rate per shift where the employer adds hours, moves the shift, or cuts it with >24 h notice; cuts with <24 h notice pay 50% of the lost hours. Changes the employee agrees to in writing (text counts) are exempt.

citation.title: Chicago Mun. Code § 6-110-050(b), (d) — Fair Workweek schedule changes
citation.excerpt: One hour of Predictability Pay for each shift in which the Employer: (A) adds hours of work. (B) changes the date or time ... (C) with more than 24 hours' notice, cancels or subtracts hours

rules.summary: A shift that starts less than 10 hours after the previous day's shift is paid at 1.25x, and the employee may decline it.

citation.title: Chicago Mun. Code § 6-110-070 — Right to rest
citation.excerpt: works a shift that begins less than 10 hours after the end of the previous day's shift ... 1.25 times the Covered Employee's regular rate

rules.summary: Chicago's minimum wage is $17.05 an hour from July 1, 2026 for employers with 4 or more employees.

citation.title: City of Chicago — Minimum Wage
citation.excerpt: As of July 1, 2026, the minimum wage in Chicago is $17.05 per hour for employers with 4 or more employees.

rules.summary: In Chicago (employers with 4+ employees) the tipped minimum wage is $12.96 an hour from July 1, 2026; if wages plus tips fall short of $17.05 the employer makes up the difference.

citation.title: City of Chicago BACP — Minimum Wage (tipped workers)
citation.excerpt: Tipped workers ... have a minimum wage of $12.96 for employers with 4 or more employees. If a tipped worker's wages plus tips do not equal at least the full minimum wage, the employer must make up the difference.

params.exception_note: Restaurants (not tavern or late-hour licenses): employees 18+ who completed Illinois Liquor Commission responsible alcohol service training may serve drinks prepared, mixed or opened by a manager or employee 21+; supermarkets: trained 18+ may stock and sell (MCC 4-60-143(a)(5), (b)).

rules.summary: In Chicago no one under 21 may handle, sell, serve or deliver alcohol at a liquor licensee, except trained servers 18+ in restaurants serving drinks a 21+ employee prepared or opened (and trained 18+ supermarket staff).

citation.title: Chicago Mun. Code § 4-60-140(a) — Liquor dealers, prohibited activities
citation.excerpt: a person under the age of 21 years ... where the sale of alcoholic liquor is not the main or principal business may not work ... in connection with the handling, selling, serving or delivering of alcoholic liquor

rules.summary: In Chicago no one under 18 may serve or sell alcohol under any exception (the restaurant and supermarket exceptions start at 18).

citation.title: Chicago Mun. Code § 4-60-143(a)(5), (b) — Hiring of persons under 21
citation.excerpt: If the licensed premises is a restaurant, an employee of the licensee who: (i) is at least 18 years of age: and (ii) obtained and completed training in basic responsible alcohol service
